key_insight: Terahertz time-domain spectroscopy can directly fingerprint and quantify specific grain-boundary defects in organic halide perovskite films, enabling non-contact defect diagnosis and guidance for passivation.
engineering_relevance: This provides a closed-loop quality-control tool for perovskite solar-cell manufacturing, linking defect identification to targeted mitigation and improved device performance.
method: Measured 0.3–3.0 THz spectra of four SVE-fabricated perovskites: MAPbI3, MAPbBr3, FAPbI3, and CsPbI3.
Matched intrinsic phonon modes and grain-boundary-localized defect vibrations to build material-specific THz fingerprints.
Used oscillator-strength analysis to quantify defect concentration and relate the 1.58 THz MAPbI3 peak to CH3NH2 defects.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the 1.58 THz absorption in MAPbI3 scales linearly with XPS-quantified CH3NH2 defect concentration, supporting THz-TDS as a direct defect meter.
watch_item: The approach depends on building reliable THz fingerprint libraries and may need careful calibration to separate overlapping defect signals across compositions and processing routes.
paper_title: Terahertz Time-Domain Spectroscopy as a Universal Defect Fingerprinting Tool for Organic Halide Perovskite Solar Cells
